trial_court: Ld. ACJ, Central, Tis Hazari Courts in Succession Case No. 231/2002
case_name: Shri Rameshwar vs Smt. Gulabi Devi

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Smt. Gulabi Devi, Through her LRs: Sh. Tara Chand, Smt. Maya Devi, and Smt. Kamlesh
parties.respondent_defendant: Shri Rameshwar, s/o Late Sh. Naval Kishore

facts_of_case: Smt. Gulabi sought grant of Succession Certificate in respect of debts and securities left by her alleged husband late Sh. Naval Kishore. Objector Rameshwar is son of late Sh. Naval Kishore and his wife Smt. Basanti Devi. He objected that petitioner was neither legally wedded wife nor widow of his father.

legal_principles.principle: Sub-succession petitions are to be decided summarily as per mandate of Section 373 Indian Succession Act, 1925.
legal_principles.held: Succession petitions only prima facie case is to be seen, whereas, complicated questions of law and fact are to be decided by regular civil court.
cited_cases: Madhavi Amma Bhawaniamma & Ors. v. Kunjikutty Pillai Minakshi Pillai & Ors., (2000) AIR SC 2301

legal_principles.principle: The grant of certificate under Section 373 Indian Succession Act, 1925 is only a determination of prima facie title.
legal_principles.held: This as a necessary corollary confirms that it is not a final decision between the parties. So, it cannot be construed that mere grant of such certificate or a decision in such proceeding would constitute to be decision on an issue finally decided between the parties.
cited_cases: Madhavi Amma Bhawaniamma & Ors. v. Kunjikutty Pillai Minakshi Pillai & Ors., (2000) AIR SC 2301

outcome.final_order: The Trial Court held that the objector, his brother Ram Dayal and three petitioners were entitled to 1/5th share each in service benefits, debts and securities of late Sh. Naval Kishore.
